---
title: "Configuration"
---

A dataset's configuration is `tether.toml` at the dataset root, committed with
the manifests and loaded into `RepoConfig`. Every key has a default; a minimal
file is just `[tether] version = 1`.

```toml
[tether]
version = 1

[snapshot]
auto = true          # CLI status/commit fingerprint by default (--no-snapshot wins)

[verify]
on_status = false    # also run a cheap verify of each committed object in status

[new]
auto_fork = false    # commit re-forks working refs from the pins it just created

[defaults]           # policy for objects added without an explicit one
write = "fork"       # fork | track
file = "immutable"   # immutable | versioned
pin = "native"       # native | record

[vcs]
prefer = "jj"        # which adapter to use when both .jj and .git exist
# jj_path = "/opt/jj/bin/jj"
# git_path = "/usr/bin/git"

[backends.file]      # passed verbatim to the backend factory; one table per kind
storage_options = { region = "us-west-2" }

[backends.neon]
api_key_env = "NEON_API_KEY"

[backends.ducklake]
init_sql = ["CREATE SECRET (TYPE S3, PROVIDER credential_chain)"]
```

## Policies

A `Policy` is stored per object (`[policy]` in its manifest) and set with the
`--write`, `--file`, `--pin` options of `tether add` or `Repo.add(policy=...)`.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write` | `fork` (default), `track` | `fork`: `new` creates a fresh per-workspace branch off the pin. `track`: the working ref is the locator's branch (e.g. `main`); use for production branches that must not be forked. |
| `file` | `immutable` (default), `versioned` | `file` backend only. `immutable`: any drift is an error at `status`. `versioned`: a single object in a versioning-enabled bucket/container is Addressable through its version id. |
| `pin` | `native` (default), `record` | Any backend. `record` drops `PIN`: `commit` records the state without creating a native ref, and `new` forks straight from the recorded state. Cheaper (no tag/branch per commit, nothing for `gc` to release) but recoverable only while the system retains that state -- `verify` reports `missing` once it is gone. See [Reclaiming storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd). |

## Import query

`[import] query` is the default SQL for `tether import` when neither `--table`
nor `--query` is given. It must yield tether's canonical columns (`key`,
`kind`, `uri` / `locator_json`, optional `policy_*`, `at`); the source (DSN or
file) is still passed on the command line, so no credentials land in the repo.
See [Registries and SQL](09-registries-and-sql.qmd).

```toml
[import]
query = "SELECT 'zarr/' || plate_name AS key, 'icechunk' AS kind, object_uri AS uri FROM data_object WHERE type = 'IcechunkStore'"
```

## Backend options

`[backends.<kind>]` is handed to the backend when it is first used. Only
non-secret settings belong here (regions, endpoints, environment-variable
*names*); credentials come from the environment. The per-backend keys are
listed in [Backends](08-backends.qmd).

## Workspace state

`.tether/workspace.toml` is untracked (ignored by the `.tether/.gitignore` that
`init` writes) and is per checkout / per jj workspace:

```toml
workspace_id = "7c1e0a4d9b2e4f6a8c1d3e5f7a9b0c2d"
base = "3ba1c07e55d2..."             # manifest hash the working refs were forked from
last_snapshot_at = "2026-09-04T22:10:03.118Z"

[working_refs]
"zarr/imaging" = "tether.ws.7c1e0a4d.zarr-imaging"
"db/metrics" = "tether.ws.7c1e0a4d.db-metrics"

[last_snapshot."zarr/imaging"]
snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"
```

`base` drives stale-working-copy detection; `working_refs` are what `open`
writes to; `last_snapshot` is what `--no-snapshot` reuses.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Read by |
| --- | --- |
| `TETHER_REV` | `Repo.open` / `tether open` default revision |
| `NEON_API_KEY` (or `[backends.neon] api_key_env`) | neon |
| `DOLT_PASSWORD`, `DOLT_USER` (or `password_env` / `user_env`) | dolt |
| AWS / GCP / Azure credential chains | file (obstore), icechunk, delta, lance |
| `LAKECTL_*` or `~/.lakectl.yaml` | lakefs |
| pyiceberg catalog properties / env | iceberg |
